title: Accelerating MoE with Dynamic In-Switch Computing on Multi-GPUs
evidence_span: Sections III-IV combine dynamic multicast/reduction addressing with token-centric fusion; V-VI evaluate simulated training and separate model-level from layer-level outcomes.
problem: Irregular expert routing creates redundant transfers and directional bandwidth imbalance.
method_or_artifact: DySHARP dynamic multimem addressing plus token-centric dispatch/computation/combine fusion.
workload_or_benchmark: DeepSeek-V3-like small/medium/large configurations; top-k 8/16/32. Main evaluation is training; larger top-k settings are exploratory.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Customized Accel-Sim plus BookSim2; simulated 32-GPU GH200 NVL32-like node, H200-based GPU configuration, nine switches. End-to-end training uses 16-way pipeline parallelism across 16 nodes.
limits: Simulation is not deployed hardware. Operator calibration does not validate all proposed hardware behavior. Layer and full-training results are distinct; numerical claims withheld pending figure/condition reconciliation. No independent review or reproduction.
